bibl.title: Cortical Membrane Potential Signature of Optimal States for Sensory Signal Detection

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: what the cortex is doing at the moment an animal is best at detecting a faint sound, and how that state can be measured continuously from outside
span.quote: We recorded membrane potentials of auditory cortical neurons in mice trained on a challenging tone-in-noise detection task while assessing arousal with simultaneous pupillometry and hippocampal recordings. Arousal measures accurately predicted multiple modes of membrane potential activity, including: rhythmic slow oscillations at low arousal, stable hyperpolarization at intermediate arousal, and depolarization during phasic or tonic periods of hyper-arousal.

span.label: what the synaptic and circuit basis is of the classical inverted-U between arousal and detection performance
span.quote: Human and animal studies have reported that performance on signal detection tasks is highly state-dependent, exhibiting an inverted-U dependence on arousal and the activity of neuromodulatory pathways. This relationship, known as the Yerkes-Dodson curve, predicts that optimal performance occurs at intermediate levels of arousal

span.label: arousal read continuously from the pupil predicts membrane potential, sensory response and behaviour, and all three are optimal at an intermediate level where the cortex is stably hyperpolarised
span.quote: Optimal signal detection behavior and sound-evoked responses, at both sub-threshold and spiking levels, occurred at intermediate arousal when pre-decision membrane potentials were stably hyperpolarized. These results reveal a cortical physiological signature of the classically-observed inverted-U relationship between task performance and arousal, and that optimal detection exhibits enhanced sensory-evoked responses and reduced background synaptic activity.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Our results suggest a cellular and network basis for this classical result.

span.label: arousal-dependent auditory signal detection
span.quote: The neural correlates of optimal states for signal detection task performance are largely unknown.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Whole cell recordings were made from regular or fast spiking neurons in layers 4 and 5 of ACtx using a physiological intracellular solution (see Supplemental Methods : Whole-Cell Recording).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: rising arousal suppresses low-frequency cortical rhythms, letting cortico-cortical and cortico-subcortical circuits interact more reliably and so producing larger, more precise sensory responses
span.quote: We hypothesize that this suppression of low frequency rhythms allows cortico-cortical and cortico-subcortical circuits to operate more reliably, enhancing sensory-evoked neuronal interactions, and thereby contributing to precise, reliable, and large sensory responses ( Haider et al., 2010 ; Lee and Dan, 2012 ; Pinto et al., 2013 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: at hyper-arousal the depolarization is carried by task-unrelated synaptic activity that raises membrane variance and thereby disrupts sensory-evoked neuronal interactions
span.quote: Although depolarization may increase the responsiveness of single cortical neurons, it may have a detrimental effect on sensory evoked neuronal interactions if the depolarization is mediated by synaptic activity that increases membrane variance or is unrelated to the task.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the opposing arousal-driven changes in thalamic gain and cortical depolarization combine to generate the U and inverted-U curves relating arousal to neural and behavioural performance
span.quote: We propose that together these opposing arousal-associated changes in thalamo-cortical activity produce the U, or inverted U, shaped relationships between neuronal and behavioral responses and arousal observed here ( Fig. 8 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the lag between cortical depolarization and pupil dilation arises because pupillary and eyelid muscles respond slowly to sympathetic and parasympathetic drive
span.quote: Much or all of this lag may represent the slow time course of pupillary/eyelid movement to alterations in sympathetic and parasympathetic activity ( Loewenfeld, 1999 ).

span.label: membrane potential and its variance trace a U-shaped relationship against arousal level as indexed by normalized pupil diameter
span.quote: Thus, plotting the membrane potential of cortical neurons as a group (n=9) against arousal level revealed a U-shaped relationship between average membrane potential/variance with normalized pupil diameter

span.label: so the signal-to-noise ratio of an evoked response is high at that state, from both suppressed background and larger responses
span.quote: At the best state for behavioral performance on our sensory detection task, the signal-to-noise ratio of evoked cortical responses is high, owing both to the suppression of spontaneous activities and the enhanced amplitude of sensory evoked responses

span.label: at high arousal the cortex depolarises, which may raise single-neuron responsiveness while degrading the interactions that carry a sensory response
span.quote: Although depolarization may increase the responsiveness of single cortical neurons, it may have a detrimental effect on sensory evoked neuronal interactions if the depolarization is mediated by synaptic activity that increases membrane variance or is unrelated to the task. The subsequent decreased reliability of cortical responses may also decrease the amplitude of their sensory-evoked responses by disrupting the optimal spatiotemporal interactions of task-related cortical circuits.

span.label: and thalamic responses fall with arousal and fall further with walking, so part of the cortical decline is inherited
span.quote: To examine if the variations in ACtx response amplitude also occurred at subcortical levels, we performed MU (n=9) recordings in the medial geniculate body (MG). As observed with ACtx neurons, variations in pupil diameter in the non-walking animal were associated with variations in the amplitude and reliability of the evoked action potential responses in MG neurons ( Fig. 5a–c ), but which were smaller in magnitude and had a distinct form. Increases in pupil diameter were associated with a steady decrease in MG response amplitude, and this response was further suppressed by a substantial amount during walking

span.label: The proposed thalamo-cortical account of the U-shaped relationship has not been tested across behavioural contexts.
span.quote: Further examination of this hypothesis, particularly the influence of behavioral context (e.g. detection vs. discrimination or exploration-exploitation tradeoffs), remains to be done.

span.label: The paper cannot resolve why locomotion enhances visual but suppresses auditory cortical responses.
span.quote: It is currently unclear whether these apparently opposing results reflect variations between sensory systems in cortical or subcortical influences of locomotion and/or arousal, or differences in the state of the animal such as the arousal level during stillness.

span.label: The neuromodulatory pathway linking pupil-indexed arousal to the cortical inhibitory circuitry was not established.
span.quote: The influence of norepinephrine, which is thought to control pupil diameter ( Aston-Jones and Cohen, 2005 ), on cortical inhibitory circuits remains to be determined.

span.label: whether the opposing visual and auditory results reflect sensory systems, subcortical influences or the arousal level during stillness is stated to be unclear
span.quote: Are the effects of arousal similar across cortical areas? In studies of the visual cortex, locomotion is associated with enhanced sensory-evoked visual responses (over non-locomotion) ( Bennett et al., 2013 ; Niell and Stryker, 2010 ; Polack et al., 2013 ), while in auditory cortex locomotion results in significant suppression of sensory evoked responses ( McGinley et al., 2013 ; Schneider et al., 2014 ; Williamson et al., 2014 ; Zhou et al., 2014 ). It is currently unclear whether these apparently opposing results reflect variations between sensory systems in cortical or subcortical influences of locomotion and/or arousal, or differences in the state of the animal such as the arousal level during stillness.

span.label: laminar position and cell type are named as a second possible source of between-study variation, with their layer 5 cells behaving unlike layer 2/3 visual cells
span.quote: Another possible source of variation between studies of locomotion or arousal effects is the laminar position and cell type of the recorded neurons. In the auditory cortex, depth of anesthesia affects pyramidal cell sensory-evoked responses and spontaneous activity differentially between cortical layers (Sakata and Harris, 2012), and the actions of neuromodulatory transmitters are layer and cell type specific (McCormick et al., 1993). Indeed, while our deep lying pyramidal neurons were depolarized during micro-arousals without walking ( Fig. 2 ), whole cell recordings from layer 2/3 pyramidal cells in the visual cortex reveal no significant change in membrane potential with non-movement related arousal

span.label: the influence of behavioural context on the proposed account remains to be done
span.quote: We propose that together these opposing arousal-associated changes in thalamo-cortical activity produce the U, or inverted U, shaped relationships between neuronal and behavioral responses and arousal observed here ( Fig. 8 ). Further examination of this hypothesis, particularly the influence of behavioral context (e.g. detection vs. discrimination or exploration-exploitation tradeoffs), remains to be done.

span.label: the peak of one measure out of thirteen, behavioural discriminability, sits at a significantly smaller pupil diameter than the rest
span.quote: The precise peak pupil diameter of the U- or inverted-U relationships differed slightly between particular behavioral and neural response measures ( Figs. 3 – 7 ). However, we did not find statistically significant difference between 12 of the 13 behavioral or physiological measures (hit rate, hit latency, d′, c, ACtx reliability, ACtx amplitude, ACtx PSP amplitude, ACtx PSP reliability, Vm minimal value, Vm rest, ACtx spontaneous, MG amplitude, MG reliability; Fig. S8 ). Only our measure of peak behavioral discriminability, d′, occurred at a significantly smaller pupil diameter than the other measures ( Fig. S8 ), possibly suggesting that optimal sound representations by auditory midbrain or brainstem structures occurs at slightly lower arousal levels than optimal thalamo-cortical processing and behavioral execution.

span.label: pupillometry as a continuous index of autonomic state, imported to index cortical membrane potential rather than emotion
span.quote: We primarily focus on pupil diameter as a measure of state, owing to its ease of measurement, non-invasive nature, and ability to continuously and sensitively track state changes, whether or not they accompany overt walking, whisking, or other movements

span.label: sharp-wave ripple rate as an independent state variable, used to validate the pupil rather than as the object of study
span.quote: The pupil diameter exhibited a strong inverse relationship to the rate of occurrence of fast ripples ( Figs. 1c–f , S1 ), with a peak coherence of 0.78 ± 0.07 (n=6 cells from N=6 animals) at low frequencies (<0.05 Hz) and a significant coherence at all frequencies up to 1 Hz ( Figs. 1e ). Theta activity was largely associated with walking ( Figs. 1c , S1b-c ). These results support the view that pupil diameter may be a useful indicator of brain state

span.label: response latency on hit trials plotted against pupil diameter, showing short latency licks and a large decrease in variability of lick latency at intermediate diameters
span.quote: Plotting response latency on hit trials versus pupil diameter, for an example session, reveals that intermediate pupil diameters are associated with short latency licks and a large decrease in variability of lick latency. e, Group data demonstrating that lick latency on hit trials is shortest for intermediate pupil diameters (n=30 sessions; N=5 animals). On false-alarm trials, lick latency from the start of the most recent TORC are significantly longer. Variability of lick latency (measured as average standard deviation) is lowest at mid pupil diameters for both hit and false alarm responses

span.label: responses sorted by state against responses averaged over all states, where no effect would be a diagonal of slope one
span.quote: If the state changes reflected by pupil diameter had no effect, this relationship would be a diagonal line with slope of 1. Variations in pupil diameter exhibited a consistent change in the slope of this relationship, with the highest slope occurring at intermediate pupil diameters ( Fig. 5d–h ) for both ACtx and MG responses (see however, ( Zhou et al., 2014 )). Smaller or larger pupil diameters away from this optimum were associated with decreases in the slope (gain) of this relationship.

span.label: eyelid opening measured IN DARKNESS, alongside the pupil recording
span.quote: To ensure that pupil dilations were not in response to changes in illumination due to eye movements, we also measured eyelid opening in darkness

span.label: pupil
span.quote: Maximal whole-cell action potential responses were evoked on trials with moderate pupil diameters ( Fig. 4a,b , S8 ; n=6). Similarly, when recorded neurons were hyperpolarized by approximately 10 mV with the intracellular injection of current to prevent action potential generation, pupil diameter significantly influenced the amplitude of stimulus evoked synaptic barrages. The largest synaptic responses were evoked at intermediate pupil diameters, with dilation or constriction from this resulting in smaller amplitude evoked synaptic responses

span.label: hyperpolarized
span.quote: As predicted, membrane potentials were most hyperpolarized (p<0.01 for hits vs. FAs) and least variable (p<0.01 for hits versus FAs) prior to hits ( Fig. 7b–d ). In addition, hit trials had the least variable membrane potentials during the early response to sound prior to onset of licking ( Fig. 7d ; p<0.05 for hits vs. misses). Finally, the amplitude of evoked synaptic responses to the onset of the auditory stimulus (tone-in-TORC) were larger for hit versus false alarm trials ( Fig. 7c ; p<0.05) Thus, we conclude that a hyperpolarized and less variable cortical membrane potential is associated with an optimal state of readiness for sensory signal detection.

span.label: evoked
span.quote: Maximal whole-cell action potential responses were evoked on trials with moderate pupil diameters ( Fig. 4a,b , S8 ; n=6). Similarly, when recorded neurons were hyperpolarized by approximately 10 mV with the intracellular injection of current to prevent action potential generation, pupil diameter significantly influenced the amplitude of stimulus evoked synaptic barrages. The largest synaptic responses were evoked at intermediate pupil diameters, with dilation or constriction from this resulting in smaller amplitude evoked synaptic responses

span.label: hit
span.quote: As predicted, membrane potentials were most hyperpolarized (p<0.01 for hits vs. FAs) and least variable (p<0.01 for hits versus FAs) prior to hits ( Fig. 7b–d ). In addition, hit trials had the least variable membrane potentials during the early response to sound prior to onset of licking ( Fig. 7d ; p<0.05 for hits vs. misses). Finally, the amplitude of evoked synaptic responses to the onset of the auditory stimulus (tone-in-TORC) were larger for hit versus false alarm trials ( Fig. 7c ; p<0.05) Thus, we conclude that a hyperpolarized and less variable cortical membrane potential is associated with an optimal state of readiness for sensory signal detection.

span.label: pupil derivative → pupil diameter
span.note: THE INDEXING / PROXY RELATION - Q-299. `from` STANDS IN FOR `to`. We have no type for it: `causes` asserts production, and `operationalised-as` says the authors CHOSE a measure, whereas a proxy claim says THIS STANDS IN FOR WHAT WE ACTUALLY CARE ABOUT AND WE KNOW IT IS NOT THE SAME THING. Measured at 8% of papers. A PROXY FOR ITSELF, DISPLACED IN TIME: 'the explanatory power of the pupil derivative occurs because IT SERVES AS A PROXY FOR THE PUPIL DIAMETER APPROXIMATELY 1 SECOND LATER'. The two endpoints are the same measurement at different lags, which is a substitution no vocabulary of concepts would catch.
span.quote: These results suggest that some, and perhaps all, of the explanatory power of the pupil derivative occurs because it serves as a proxy for the pupil diameter approximately 1 second later.

span.label: A LITERATURE'S CONTRADICTIONS ATTRIBUTED TO A VARIABLE NOBODY MEASURED: state fluctuates continuously and in seconds, which produces variability between studies and between moments inside one study, and has not been accounted for
span.quote: One possible explanation of these apparently divergent results is that state (arousal) fluctuates continuously and rapidly, resulting in a high degree of variability between studies and between moments within individual studies, which has not been accounted for.

span.label: and one earlier report is named as having recorded across un-anaesthetised states without quantifying the arousal of the animals at all
span.quote: Membrane potentials in auditory cortex of rats have been found to be hyperpolarized and inactive across un-anesthetized states, though the arousal level of the animals was not quantified

span.label: A BINARY CATEGORY IS DISSOLVED INTO A CONTINUUM: the same pupil measure had been used to sort trials into aroused and unaroused, and is used here as a graded quantity
span.quote: Indeed, in rodents, measures of the pupil diameter have been used for binary classification of ‘aroused’ or ‘unaroused’ states and predict differences in sensory response magnitude and reliability and the extent of slow fluctuations in visual cortical membrane potential

span.label: AND A WHOLE LITERATURE'S INDEPENDENT VARIABLE IS RE-IDENTIFIED: the often reported effects of movement may not result from movement per se but from arousal, with one exception named and kept
span.quote: Indeed, our results indicate that the often reported effects of movement may not result from movement (e.g. whisking or walking), per se, but rather from arousal. In our animals, walking necessarily involved strong arousal (pupil dilation) and we observed largely similar effects on neural responses and behavioral performance of high arousal during either stillness or walking ( Figs. 2 – 6 ), with the exception of an arousal-independent walking effect on thalamic sound responses and decision bias.

span.label: THE SHAPE OF THE EFFECT BREAKS THE SUMMARY STATISTIC: because the relation is U-shaped the correlation is positive over one half of the range and negative over the other, which forced a sliding window rather than one coefficient
span.quote: The U-shaped relationship between Vm and pupil diameter resulted in a positive correlation between pupil diameter and Vm for intermediate to highly aroused states, and a negative correlation between these measures at unaroused to intermediate arousal levels. This correlation pattern necessitated use of a sliding window when calculating Vm-to-pupil coherence

span.label: A RIVAL MEASURE IS TESTED AND THEN EXPLAINED AWAY: the derivative of the pupil predicts less than the diameter, and correlates with the diameter a second later, so its explanatory power may be entirely borrowed
span.quote: Importantly, we found that the derivative of the pupil was correlated to the pupil diameter 1.3 ± 0.7 seconds later (CC = 0.32 ± 0.02; p<0.001; n=9; Fig. S6k,l ), but not to the pupil diameter at the same time (correlation coefficient CC = 0.0035 ± 0.0043; p=0.44). This lag approximately matched the observed lag between physiological activity and pupil diameter (see e.g. Fig. 2b,c and Methods), which reflects neural and muscle activation delays in the control of the pupil ( Loewenfeld, 1999 ). These results suggest that some, and perhaps all, of the explanatory power of the pupil derivative occurs because it serves as a proxy for the pupil diameter approximately 1 second later. This is particularly the case during micro-dilations, when the pupil diameter fluctuates on approximately the same time scale (e.g. seconds) as the pupillary lag

span.label: THE MEASURE IS VALIDATED THROUGH A CHANNEL WHERE THE CONFOUND CANNOT OPERATE: pupil dilation could be a response to light, so eyelid opening was measured in darkness, where dilation is saturated, and moved the same way
span.quote: To ensure that pupil dilations were not in response to changes in illumination due to eye movements, we also measured eyelid opening in darkness ( Fig. S2 ), since eyelid opening and pupil diameter are coupled together through co-innervation by the sympathetic nervous system ( Loewenfeld, 1999 ). As expected, pupil dilation and eyelid opening fluctuated coherently, such that even in darkness (where pupil dilation is saturated), eyelid opening exhibited the same slow changes associated with walking or disengagement and micro-openings that are characteristic of pupil diameter

span.label: and the recording artefact is ruled out by timing rather than by argument - the depolarisation begins before the behavioural event and returns after it
span.quote: The changes in membrane potential we observed in cortical neurons with pupil dilations or walking did not result from disruptions of recording quality, since the membrane potential depolarization initiated prior to each behavioral event (e.g. dilation or walking) and always returned to pre-movement levels once movement or arousal ceased.

span.label: THIRTEEN MEASURES ARE ASKED WHETHER THEY PEAK IN THE SAME PLACE: twelve are statistically indistinguishable and the thirteenth is not, with an interpretation offered for the one
span.quote: The precise peak pupil diameter of the U- or inverted-U relationships differed slightly between particular behavioral and neural response measures ( Figs. 3 – 7 ). However, we did not find statistically significant difference between 12 of the 13 behavioral or physiological measures (hit rate, hit latency, d′, c, ACtx reliability, ACtx amplitude, ACtx PSP amplitude, ACtx PSP reliability, Vm minimal value, Vm rest, ACtx spontaneous, MG amplitude, MG reliability; Fig. S8 ). Only our measure of peak behavioral discriminability, d′, occurred at a significantly smaller pupil diameter than the other measures ( Fig. S8 ), possibly suggesting that optimal sound representations by auditory midbrain or brainstem structures occurs at slightly lower arousal levels than optimal thalamo-cortical processing and behavioral execution.

span.label: and the state measure is normalised within session because its maximum drifts between days and animals, so every number here is a fraction of that animal's own range
span.quote: The maximal pupil diameter achieved during each recording or behavioral session always occurred walking and varied, slightly, from day to day and animal to animal. Thus, to facilitate population-level comparisons and analysis, we normalized the pupil diameter by dividing by its maximal value in each session

span.label: extends → Reimer et al. (2014)
span.quote: A recently published study of the mouse visual cortex, which paralleled our own investigations, suggested that the rate of change of pupil diameter was an accurate measure of changes in cortical membrane potential power ( Reimer et al., 2014 ).

span.label: contradicts → Reimer et al. (2014)
span.quote: Indeed, while our deep lying pyramidal neurons were depolarized during micro-arousals without walking ( Fig. 2 ), whole cell recordings from layer 2/3 pyramidal cells in the visual cortex reveal no significant change in membrane potential with non-movement related arousal ( Reimer et al., 2014 ).

span.label: replicates → Williamson et al. (2014)
span.quote: These results are consistent with the large walking-specific decrease in evoked firing rate in MG neurons ( Fig. 5b ) ( Williamson et al., 2014 ).

span.label: explains-away → the rate of change of pupil diameter as the better index of cortical state, which is shown to be a lagged proxy for the diameter itself
span.quote: Importantly, we found that the derivative of the pupil was correlated to the pupil diameter 1.3 ± 0.7 seconds later (CC = 0.32 ± 0.02; p<0.001; n=9; Fig. S6k,l ), but not to the pupil diameter at the same time (correlation coefficient CC = 0.0035 ± 0.0043; p=0.44). This lag approximately matched the observed lag between physiological activity and pupil diameter (see e.g. Fig. 2b,c and Methods), which reflects neural and muscle activation delays in the control of the pupil ( Loewenfeld, 1999 ). These results suggest that some, and perhaps all, of the explanatory power of the pupil derivative occurs because it serves as a proxy for the pupil diameter approximately 1 second later. This is particularly the case during micro-dilations, when the pupil diameter fluctuates on approximately the same time scale (e.g. seconds) as the pupillary lag

span.label: reconciles → the divergent reports of cortical membrane potential in waking animals, by supplying the continuously varying state variable none of them measured
span.quote: One possible explanation of these apparently divergent results is that state (arousal) fluctuates continuously and rapidly, resulting in a high degree of variability between studies and between moments within individual studies, which has not been accounted for.

span.label: critiques → studies of the effects of walking and whisking on sensory responses, which most likely involved large uncontrolled changes in arousal
span.quote: Owing to the association of walking with large pupil diameter that we observed, previous studies on the effects of walking or other movements on sensory responses have most likely involved significant changes in arousal

span.label: supports → the classical Yerkes-Dodson inverted-U between arousal and performance, by giving it a cellular and network basis
span.quote: Our results suggest a cellular and network basis for this classical result. We found that intermediate arousal, as measured by pupillometry and hippocampal state, corresponded to a low noise cortical state and optimal behavioral performance in a tone-in-noise detection task and thalamic and cortical sound responses. At intermediate arousal, behavioral performance was most rapid and accurate, sensory responses were largest and most reliable at both the spiking and subthreshold membrane potential levels, and spontaneous cortical membrane potentials were stably hyperpolarized.

span.label: qualifies → the opposing visual and auditory locomotion results, which are left explicitly unresolved
span.quote: Are the effects of arousal similar across cortical areas? In studies of the visual cortex, locomotion is associated with enhanced sensory-evoked visual responses (over non-locomotion) ( Bennett et al., 2013 ; Niell and Stryker, 2010 ; Polack et al., 2013 ), while in auditory cortex locomotion results in significant suppression of sensory evoked responses ( McGinley et al., 2013 ; Schneider et al., 2014 ; Williamson et al., 2014 ; Zhou et al., 2014 ). It is currently unclear whether these apparently opposing results reflect variations between sensory systems in cortical or subcortical influences of locomotion and/or arousal, or differences in the state of the animal such as the arousal level during stillness.

span.note: A LITERATURE'S CONTRADICTIONS ATTRIBUTED TO A VARIABLE NOBODY MEASURED: it fluctuates continuously and rapidly, producing variability between studies and between moments within one, and has not been accounted for
span.quote: One possible explanation of these apparently divergent results is that state (arousal) fluctuates continuously and rapidly, resulting in a high degree of variability between studies and between moments within individual studies, which has not been accounted for.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE FIELD'S DISAGREEMENT, PLUS THE VIEW THIS PAPER COMPLICATES) · state —causes→ membrane potential
span.note: RETRACTED: THE FIELD'S DISAGREEMENT, PLUS THE VIEW THIS PAPER COMPLICATES. The span: 'Reports on the cortical membrane potential dynamics associated with wakeful states HAVE COME TO WIDELY DIFFERING CONCLUSION between species and sensory systems. Wakefulness is TRADITIONALLY ASSOCIATED with low amplitude and arrhythmic scalp EEG. THIS CANONICAL...' - the first sentence says the literature does not agree and the second states the canonical view. The paper's own finding is that the relationship is non-monotonic in arousal, which is why the canonical account is quoted here at all. A reader joining on `X --causes--> Y` takes it as a causal relation this paper reports. Q-395. — and the reports it is meant to reconcile came to widely differing conclusions between species and sensory systems
span.quote: Reports on the cortical membrane potential dynamics associated with wakeful states have come to widely differing conclusion between species and sensory systems. Wakefulness is traditionally associated with low amplitude and arrhythmic scalp EEG. This canonical wakeful state has been referred to as the ‘activated’ or ‘asynchronous’ state, because excitatory neurons are thought to be tonically depolarized while interacting in a manner that reduces broad-ranging synchrony ( Renart et al., 2010 ; Steriade et al., 2001 ; van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky, 1996 ). Membrane potential recordings in awake cats support this view ( Steriade et al., 2001 ), but recent work in rodent sensory cortical areas has revealed additional complexity.

span.label: RETRACTED (`anesthe` IS NOT A TERM - see Kato2015[0]) · arousal —distinct-from→ anesthe
span.note: RETRACTED: `anesthe` IS NOT A TERM - see Kato2015[0]. Here it is attested by `un-anesthetized`, which is additionally the NEGATION of what the endpoint appears to mean. — one earlier report recorded across un-anaesthetised states without quantifying arousal at all - the variable was not absent, it was unmeasured
span.quote: Membrane potentials in auditory cortex of rats have been found to be hyperpolarized and inactive across un-anesthetized states, though the arousal level of the animals was not quantified

span.note: chosen for being non-invasive and continuous, and for tracking state changes whether or not they come with overt movement

span.note: validated against an independent central signal before it is used for anything - a strong inverse relation to hippocampal ripple rate

span.note: THE CONFOUND IS REMOVED BY CHANGING CHANNEL: dilation could be a response to light, so eyelid opening was measured in darkness, where dilation is saturated, and moved the same way
span.quote: To ensure that pupil dilations were not in response to changes in illumination due to eye movements, we also measured eyelid opening in darkness ( Fig. S2 ), since eyelid opening and pupil diameter are coupled together through co-innervation by the sympathetic nervous system ( Loewenfeld, 1999 ). As expected, pupil dilation and eyelid opening fluctuated coherently, such that even in darkness (where pupil dilation is saturated), eyelid opening exhibited the same slow changes associated with walking or disengagement and micro-openings that are characteristic of pupil diameter

span.label: EIS —operationalised-as→ eyelid
span.note: and a cheaper proxy is then derived from the light reflected off the eye, so the measure can travel
span.quote: We also found that an easily-measured proxy for changes in lid opening and pupil diameter is the amount of light reflected from the eye from an infrared light source, a measure we term eye-indexed state (EIS; Figs. 2a,b , S2 ; N=7). These results indicate that pupil dilation in constant illumination, eyelid opening in the dark, or EIS in either condition, are precise, accurate, and easily obtained, measures of brain state.

span.label: pupil —contrasted-with→ derivative
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHICH PREDICTOR ADDS ANYTHING, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT ONE DOES NOT. 'FACTORING IN BOTH THE PUPIL DIAMETER AND ITS DERIVATIVE explained 40+/-6% of the variance of power in the 2-10 Hz band, WHICH WAS STATISTICALLY LARGER THAN THE AMOUNT EXPLAINED BY PUPIL DERIVATIVE (p<0.0005), BUT NOT PUPIL DIAMETER ALONE (p=0.36).' Adding the derivative to diameter does not improve on diameter alone - a null reported in the same sentence as the significant comparison, and the pair is only distinguishable because both tests are given. Q-473. — A RIVAL MEASURE TESTED HEAD TO HEAD: the diameter explains 34 percent of the variance in low-frequency power, the derivative about half that, and both together add nothing over the diameter alone
span.quote: To test whether pupil diameter or the rate of change of pupil diameter was a better indicator of rhythmic membrane potential activities, we compared both 1) raw pupil diameter and 2) the rate of change of pupil diameter to membrane power at 2–10 Hz and other frequency bands ( Figs. S5, S6 and Supplementary Table ). We found that pupil diameter explained 34±7% (n=9) of the variance in dB power at low frequencies (2–10 Hz), while the rate of change (temporal derivative) of pupil diameter explained approximately half as much variance (18±4%; p<0.005; F 1,7 =28.3, group p<0.001). Factoring in both the pupil diameter and its derivative explained 40±6% of the variance of power in the 2–10 Hz band, which was statistically larger than the amount explained by pupil derivative (p<0.0005), but not pupil diameter alone (p=0.36).

span.label: derivative —distinct-from→ pupil
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS TEMPORAL LAG, AND BOTH CORRELATIONS ARE GIVEN. 'THE DERIVATIVE OF THE PUPIL WAS CORRELATED TO THE PUPIL DIAMETER 1.3 +/- 0.7 SECONDS LATER (CC = 0.32 +/- 0.02; p<0.001), BUT NOT TO THE PUPIL DIAMETER AT THE SAME TIME (CC = 0.0035 +/- 0.0043; p=0.44).' The same two quantities are unrelated at lag zero and strongly related at 1.3 s - so a study measuring them concurrently would report independence, and the paper goes on to attribute the lag to muscle and neural delays in pupil control. Q-473. — AND THEN EXPLAINED AWAY: the derivative correlates with the diameter 1.3 s later and not with the diameter at the same moment, so some and perhaps all of its power is borrowed
